subject.title: fix(auto-reply): hide recovered failed tool progress

question: Should regular verbose mode hide failed tool progress after any confirmed visible non-error reply, or should recovery-aware hiding remain opt-in so failed side effects stay visible by default?
rationale: The implementation cannot establish that a later successful-looking response means every failed side effect was actually recovered; choosing warning visibility is a shared safety and UX policy decision.

options.title: Keep fail-visible default
options.body: Close this PR and retain visible warnings unless an operator explicitly selects suppression or a future recovery-aware mode.

options.title: Sponsor shared hiding
options.body: Approve the PR's new default, then reopen or refresh it with exact-head and native channel validation.

options.title: Design opt-in policy
options.body: Preserve current behavior by default and add recovery-aware delivery only after approving the additional configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-visible default
recommendation.body: Close this PR and retain visible warnings unless an operator explicitly selects suppression or a future recovery-aware mode.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the recent shared dispatch and follow-up delivery structure and is best positioned to decide the cross-channel default with warning-policy contributors.
